items.question: What is the difference between pencil, ink and colour pencil?
items.answer:
Pencil is traditional. I'm more comfortable and faster with pencil, so if you ask me to choose I'll choose pencil. It suits every portrait and every animal.

Ink is a different style. I paint the ink on with a brush and then add details with ink pens, and the process takes longer. Occasionally, on seeing your photo, I might decide it isn't suited to ink, though this seldom happens.

Colour pencil is built up in many fine layers to capture your pet's true colouring. It needs a clear, well-lit photo so I can see the real colours of the fur and eyes.

- It's a subjective choice. If you're unsure, choose pencil.

items.question: What size should I choose?
items.answer:
- Look at your space and decide what size will look best and fit.
- If your photo isn't the best quality, I'd suggest a smaller size.
- Two pets on one page: A4 or A3.
- Just the head and neck: A5 or A4.
- The whole body: A4 or A3.

items.question: What photo should I choose?
items.answer:
Send me your top three if you can't choose. I'll pick one based on crop and detail and make a digital layout so you can see how it will look. I can do up to three layouts, but I can't try layouts for fifty photos.

Choose the photo that looks most like your pet, with the most detail. Send the original file rather than a screenshot. If the photo is blurred, the drawing will be too. I draw only what I see.

items.question: How long will it take?
items.answer: It depends on the artwork, medium, size and my waiting list. When I'm quiet it can take about two weeks; when I'm busy, five to eight weeks. A portrait can never go from email to your door within a week, as commission prep and correspondence take time.

items.question: Can I ask for changes?
items.answer: Yes, within reason. Most of the time I can see what you see and will happily make a change or two. I may decline millimetre-level changes that don't make a visible difference.
